chunks.arabic_text: إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ مِهْرَانَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ، السَّكُونِيُّ، يُكْنَى أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ. لَيْسَ حَدِيثِيهِ بِالنَّقِيِّ، يَضْطَرِبُ تَارَةً وَيَصْلُحُ أُخْرَى. وَيَرْوِي عَنِ الضُّعَفَاءِ كَثِيرًا، وَيُجَازُ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ شَاهِدًا.

translations.en: Ismāʿīl b. Mihrān b. Muḥammad b. Abī Naṣr, al-Sakūnī, known by the kunya Abū Muḥammad. His ḥadīths are not pure, sometimes they are disturbed, and others are upright. He narrates from weak narrators a lot. It is permissible to bring his (ḥadīth) out as a witness.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitab al-Du'afā'* characterizes Ismāʿīl ibn Mihrān al-Sakūnī as a narrator of mixed reliability, whose occasional instability (*idtirāb*) prevents his hadith from serving as independent proof (*hujjah*). However, his narrations remain valid for corroboration (*shahāda*) when supported by other chains, reflecting the nuanced Shia approach to evaluating secondary narrators. This classification highlights the practical application of *jarḥ wa taʿdīl* (criticism and validation) in preserving the integrity of the hadith corpus.
en.seo_question: What is the status of Ismāʿīl ibn Mihrān al-Sakūnī in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.النَّقِيِّ: Pure/Flawless (referring to the quality of a narrator's hadith)
key_terms.يَضْطَرِبُ: He is disturbed/unstable (referring to inconsistencies in narration)
key_terms.شَاهِدًا: As a witness/corroboration (a lower level of evidentiary weight than hujjah)
